unit.reading: Apocalypse of Moses. Narrative and way of life of Adam and Eve, the first-formed, revealed by God to Moses his servant, when he received the tablets of the law of the covenant from the hand of the Lord, having been instructed by the archangel Michael.

Apocalypse of Moses. Narrative and way of life of Adam and Eve, the first-formed, revealed by God to Moses his servant, when he received the tablets of the law of the covenant from the hand of the Lord, having been instructed by the archangel Michael.

This is the narrative of Adam and Eve. After they went out from paradise, Adam took Eve his wife and went up to the east. And he remained there eighteen years and two months, and Eve conceived and gave birth to two sons, Diaphotos, who was called Cain, and Amilabes, who was called Abel.

And after these things, Adam and Eve were together. While they were sleeping, Eve said to her lord Adam, 'My lord, in a dream this night I saw the blood of my son Amilabes, who is called Abel, being poured into the mouth of Cain his brother, and he drank it mercilessly. And he begged him to leave him a little of it, but he did not listen to him, but swallowed it completely; and it did not remain in his stomach, but came out of his mouth.' Then Adam said to Eve, 'Let us arise and go and see what has happened to them, lest the enemy should somehow be waging war against them.'

And when they had gone, they both found Abel murdered by the hand of Cain his brother. And God said to Michael the archangel, 'Say to Adam: "Do not disclose to Cain your son the mystery which you know, for he is a son of wrath. But do not grieve, for I will give you another son in his place; he will reveal to you everything you are to do for him, but you must tell him nothing."' God said these things to his angel, and Adam kept the word in his heart, and Eve with him, while they bore grief concerning Abel their son.

And after these things Adam knew his wife, and she conceived and gave birth to Seth. And Adam said to Eve, 'Behold, we have begotten a son in place of Abel, whom Cain killed; let us give glory and a sacrifice to God.'

And Adam had thirty sons and thirty daughters. And having fallen into illness, he cried out with a loud voice and said, 'Let all my sons come to me, so that I may see them before I die.' And they were all gathered together—for the earth had been inhabited in three parts—and they all came to the door of the house in which he used to enter to pray to God. And Seth his son said, 'Father Adam, what is your illness?' And he said, 'My children, great pain grips me.' And they said, 'What is pain and illness?'

And answering, Seth said to him, 'Father, did you remember paradise, from which you used to eat, and were you grieved desiring it? If it is so, tell me, and I will go and bring you fruit from paradise. For I will put dung upon my head and weep and pray, and the Lord will hear me and send his angel, and I will bring it to you so that the pain may cease from you.' Adam said to him, 'No, my son Seth, but I have an illness and pain.' Seth said to him, 'And how did they happen to you?'

And Adam said to him, 'When God made us, me and your mother, on whose account I also am dying, he gave us every plant in paradise, but concerning one he commanded us not to eat from it, on account of which we are also dying. And the hour drew near for the angels who guarded your mother to go up and worship the Lord; and the enemy gave to her and she ate from the tree, knowing that I was not near her, nor were the holy angels; then she gave to me also to eat.'

And when we both had eaten, God was angry with us. And the Master, having come into paradise, set up his throne and called out with a terrible voice, saying, 'Adam, where are you? And why do you hide from my face? Can a house be hidden from the one who built it?' And he said, 'Because you abandoned my covenant, I have brought upon your body seventy plagues. The pain of the first plague is the violent strain of the eyes; the second plague is the pain of hearing; and so in turn all the plagues shall follow you.'

And saying these things to his sons, Adam groaned greatly and said, 'What shall I do? I am in great sorrow.' And Eve also wept, saying, 'My lord Adam, rise up, give me half of your illness, and I will endure it, because this happened to you on my account; on my account you are beset with labors and pains.' But Adam said to Eve, 'Arise and go with our son Seth near paradise, and put earth upon your heads and weep, begging God that he might have compassion on me and send his angel into paradise and give me from the tree from which oil flows, and that you may bring it to me, and I will anoint myself and have rest, and I will explain to you the way in which we were deceived at the first.'

And Seth and Eve went toward the regions of paradise. And as they were going, Eve saw her son and a wild beast attacking him. And Eve wept, saying, 'Woe is me, woe is me! For if I come to the day of resurrection, all who have sinned will curse me, saying that Eve did not keep the commandment of God.' And Eve cried out to the wild beast, saying, 'O you wicked beast, are you not afraid to fight against the image of God? How was your mouth opened? How were your teeth strengthened? How did you not remember your subjection, that previously you were subjected to the image of God?'

Then the wild beast cried out, saying, 'O Eve, your greed and your weeping are not against us, but against yourself, since the beginning of the beasts came from you. How was your mouth opened to eat from the tree concerning which God commanded you not to eat from it? On this account our nature also was altered. Now therefore you will not be able to endure if I begin to rebuke you.'

Then Seth said to the beast, 'Close your mouth and be silent, and stand back from the image of God until the day of judgment.' Then the beast said to Seth, 'Behold, I stand back, Seth, from the image of God.' Then the beast fled and left him wounded, and went to its dwelling.'

And Seth went with his mother Eve near paradise; and they wept there, begging God that he would send his angel and give them the oil of mercy. And God sent to them Michael the archangel, and he spoke to them these words: 'Seth, man of God, do not labor praying with this supplication concerning the tree from which the oil flows, to anoint your father Adam; for it will not happen for you now, but at the end of times. Then all flesh shall rise from Adam until that great day, as many as will be a holy people; then all the joy of paradise will be given to them, and God will be in their midst; and they will no longer sin before him, because the evil heart will be taken away from them, and a heart understanding what is good and serving God alone will be given to them. But go back to your father, since the measure of his life has been completed, equal to three days; and when his soul goes out, you are about to behold its fearful ascent.'

And having said these things, the angel departed from them. Seth and Eve came to the tent where Adam was lying. And Adam said to Eve, 'What have you wrought among us and brought upon us great wrath, which is death ruling over all our race?' And he said to her, 'Call all our children and the children of our children, and declare to them the manner of our transgression.'

Then Eve said to them, 'Listen, all my children and the children of my children, and I will declare to you how our enemy deceived us. It happened while we were guarding paradise, each of us was guarding the portion allotted to him from God; and I was guarding in my lot the south and the west. But the devil went to the lot of Adam, where the male wild beasts were; since God divided the wild beasts between us, and he gave all the males to your father, and all the females he gave to me, and each of us was watching his own.'

And the devil spoke to the serpent, saying, 'Arise, come to me, and I will tell you a word by which you may benefit.' Then the serpent came to him, and the devil said to him, 'I hear that you are wiser than all the wild beasts, and I came to observe you; and I found you greater than all the wild beasts, and they associate with you; yet you bow down to the least. Why do you eat from the tares of Adam and his wife, and not from the fruit of paradise? Arise and come, and let us cause him to be cast out through his wife from paradise, just as we also were cast out on his account.' The serpent said to him, 'I fear lest the Lord should be angry with me.' The devil said to him, 'Do not fear; only become a vessel for me, and I will speak through your mouth a word by which you will be able to deceive him.'

And immediately he hung over the walls of paradise around the hour when the angels of God went up to worship. Then Satan took the form of an angel and sang hymns to God just as the angels; and looking out from the wall I saw him like an angel. And he said to me, 'Are you Eve?' And I said to him, 'I am.' And he said to me, 'What are you doing in paradise?' And I said to him, 'God placed us to guard it and to eat from it.' The devil answered me through the mouth of the serpent, 'You do well, but you do not eat from every plant.' And I said to him, 'Yes, from every plant we eat except one only, which is in the midst of paradise, concerning which God commanded us not to eat from it, for you shall surely die by death.'

Then the serpent said to me, 'As God lives, I am grieved concerning you, because you are like cattle. For I do not want you to be ignorant of this, but arise, come here, listen to me and eat, and perceive the value of the tree.' But I said to him, 'I fear lest God should be angry with me, just as he told us.' And he said to me, 'Do not fear; for as soon as you eat, your eyes will be opened, and you will be like gods in knowing what is good and what is evil. And God, knowing this, that you would be like him, envied you and said, "You shall not eat from it." But pay attention to the plant, and you will see great glory concerning it.' And I paid attention to the plant, and I saw great glory concerning it. But I said to him that it was beautiful to behold with the eyes, yet I feared to take from the fruit. And he said to me, 'Come, I will give to you; follow me.'

And I opened to him, and he entered inside into paradise, and walked before me. And having walked a little, he turned and said to me, 'I have changed my mind; I will not give you to eat.' But he said these things wishing to entice and destroy me to the end. And he said to me, 'Swear to me that you will also give to your husband.' And I said to him, 'I do not know by what oath I should swear to you, but what I know I say to you: by the throne of the Master and the cherubim and the tree of life, I will also give to my husband to eat.' And when he received the oath from me, then he went and climbed upon it; and he placed upon the fruit which he gave me to eat the poison of his wickedness, that is, of his desire; for desire is the head of all sin. And I bent the branch to the ground and took from the fruit and ate.

And in that very hour my eyes were opened, and I knew that I was naked of the righteousness with which I had been clothed. And I wept, saying, 'Why have you done this to me, that I have been alienated from my glory with which I had been clothed?' And I also wept concerning the oath. But he came down from the plant and vanished. And I searched in my region for leaves so that I might cover my shame, and I found none from the plants of paradise, since, as soon as I ate, the leaves fell from all the plants of my region except the fig tree alone. And having taken leaves from it, I made aprons for myself, and it is from the very plants from which I ate.

And I cried out with a loud voice, saying, 'Adam, Adam, where are you? Arise, come to me, and I will show you a great mystery.' And when your father came, I spoke to him words of transgression, which brought us down from great glory. For as soon as he came, I opened my mouth and the devil was speaking, and I began to admonish him, saying, 'Come, my lord Adam, listen to me and eat from the fruit of the tree of which God told us not to eat from it, and you will be like God.' And answering, your father said, 'I fear lest God should be angry with me.' But I said to him, 'Do not fear; for as soon as you eat, you will know good and evil.' And then, having quickly persuaded him, he ate, and his eyes were opened, and he too knew his nakedness. And he said to me, 'O wicked woman, what have you wrought among us? You have alienated me from the glory of God.'

And in that very hour we heard the archangel Michael sounding his trumpet, calling the angels, saying, 'Thus says the Lord: Come with me into paradise and hear the word by which I judge Adam.' And when we heard the archangel sounding the trumpet, we said, 'Behold, God is coming into paradise to judge us.' And we were afraid and hid ourselves. And God ascended into paradise, mounted upon a chariot of Cherubim, with the angels praising him. When God entered into paradise, all the plants both of the lot of Adam and of my lot blossomed and stood upright, and the throne of God was prepared where the tree of life was.

And God called Adam, saying, 'Adam, where have you hidden, thinking that I will not find you? Can a house be hidden from the one who built it?' Then your father answered and said, 'No, Lord, we do not hide thinking that we are not found by you, but I am afraid, because I am naked, and I feared your power, Master.' God said to him, 'Who showed you that you are naked, unless you have abandoned my commandment which I gave you to keep?' Then Adam remembered the word which I spoke to him when I wished to deceive him, 'I will make you secure from God'; and turning to me he said to me, 'Why did you do this?' And I too remembered the word of the serpent, and I said, 'The serpent deceived me.'

God said to Adam, 'Because you disobeyed my commandment and listened to your wife, cursed is the ground in your labors; for whenever you cultivate it, it will not give its strength, thorns and thistles it will bring forth for you, and in the sweat of your face you will eat your bread. And you shall be in many kinds of labors: you shall labor and not rest, afflicted by bitterness and not tasting sweetness, afflicted by heat and constrained by cold; and you shall toil much and not become rich, and you shall grow fat yet in the end you will not exist, and the wild beasts over which you ruled will rise up against you in rebellion, because you did not keep my commandment.'

And turning to me the Lord said to me, 'Because you listened to the serpent and disobeyed my commandment, you shall be in distress and in unbearable pains; you shall bear children in much trembling, and in one hour you shall come near to lose your life from your great distress and pangs. But you will confess and say, "Lord, Lord, save me, and I will never return to the sin of the flesh." And on account of this, by your own word I will judge you, because of the enmity which the enemy placed in you; and you shall turn again to your husband, and he shall rule over you.'

And after saying these things to me, he spoke to the serpent in great wrath, saying to him, 'Because you did this and became an ungrateful vessel until you deceived the careless in heart, cursed are you above all cattle; you shall be deprived of the food which you used to eat, and dust you shall eat all the days of your life; upon your breast and belly you shall go, and you shall be deprived of both your hands and your feet; neither ear nor wing nor one limb of all those with which you enticed in your wickedness and caused them to be cast out from paradise shall be left to you; and I will put enmity between you and between his seed; he shall watch for your head, and you for his heel, until the day of judgment.'

And having said these things, he commanded his angels that we be cast out from paradise. And as we were being driven out and lamenting, your father Adam begged the angels, saying, 'Allow me a little while so that I may plead with God, and he may have compassion and pity on me, for I alone sinned.' And they ceased driving him; and Adam cried out with weeping, saying, 'Pardon me, Lord, for what I have done.' Then the Lord said to his angels, 'Why have you ceased driving Adam from paradise? Is the sin mine, or have I judged badly?' Then the angels, falling upon the ground, worshiped the Lord, saying, 'You are righteous, Lord, and you judge with uprightness.'

And turning to Adam, the Lord said, 'I will not permit you from now on to be in paradise.' And answering, Adam said, 'Lord, give me from the plant of life that I may eat before I am cast out.' Then the Lord spoke to Adam, 'You shall not take from it now; for it was appointed to the Cherubim and the flaming sword that turns about to guard it on your account, so that you might not taste of it and be immortal forever, having the warfare which the enemy placed in you. But when you go out from paradise, if you guard yourself from all evil as one willing to die, when the resurrection takes place again, I will raise you up, and then it will be given to you from the tree of life, and you will be immortal forever.'

And having said these things, the Lord commanded that we be cast out from paradise. And your father wept before the angels opposite paradise, and the angels said to him, 'What do you want us to do for you, Adam?' And your father answered and said to the angels, 'Behold, you are casting me out; I beg you, allow me to take sweet fragrances from paradise, so that after I go out I may offer a sacrifice to God, that God may hear me.' And the angels approached and said to God, 'Jael, eternal King, command that sweet-smelling incenses from paradise be given to Adam.' And God commanded Adam to come, that he might take sweet spices from paradise for his sustenance. And when the angels permitted him, he gathered both kinds: saffron, and nard, and sweet cane, and cinnamon, and other seeds for his sustenance; and having taken these, he went out from paradise. And we came to be upon the earth.
Now therefore, my children, I have revealed to you the way in which we were deceived; but guard yourselves not to abandon what is good.

And having said these things in the midst of her sons, while Adam was sleeping in his illness—and he had one more day before departing from the body—Eve said to Adam, 'Why are you dying and I am living? Or how much time do I have to spend after you die? Tell me.' Then Adam said to Eve, 'Do not be anxious about matters; for you will not delay after me, but we both shall die equally, and you yourself will be laid in my place. And when I die, leave me, and let no one touch me until the angel of the Lord shall say something concerning me; for God will not forget me, but will seek out his own vessel which he fashioned. Rather arise, pray to God until I give up my spirit into the hands of the one who gave it; because we do not know how we will meet the one who made us, whether he will be angry with us or turn to have mercy on us.'

Then Eve arose and went outside, and falling upon the earth she said, 'I have sinned, O God, I have sinned, O Father of all, I have sinned against you, I have sinned against your chosen angels, I have sinned against the Cherubim, I have sinned against your unshakable throne, I have sinned, Lord, I have sinned greatly, I have sinned before you, and all sin has occurred through me in the creation.' And while Eve was still praying upon her knees, behold, the angel of humanity came to her and raised her up, saying, 'Arise, Eve, from your repentance; for behold, Adam your husband has departed from his body. Arise and see his spirit being carried up to the one who made it, to meet him.'

And having arisen, Eve put her hand upon her face, and the angel said to her, 'Lift yourself up from earthly things.' And Eve gazed into heaven, and saw a chariot of light coming, drawn by four bright eagles—whose glory it was not possible for anyone born of a womb to tell, nor to see their face—and angels preceding the chariot. When they came to the place where your father Adam was lying, the chariot stopped, and the Seraphim were between the father and the chariot. And I saw golden censers and three bowls, and behold, all the angels with frankincense and the censers and the bowls came to the altar and blew upon them, and the smoke of the incense covered the firmaments. And the angels fell down and worshiped God, crying out and saying, 'Holy Jael, pardon, for he is your image and the work of your holy hands.'

And again, I, Eve, saw two great and fearful mysteries standing before God. And I wept out of fear, and I cried out to my son Seth, saying, 'Arise, Seth, from the body of your father Adam and come to me, so that you may see what no one's eye has ever seen, and how they are interceding on behalf of your father Adam.'

Then Seth arose and came to his mother and said to her, 'What is the matter with you? And why are you weeping?' She said to him, 'Look up with your eyes and see the seven firmaments opened, and see with your eyes how the body of your father lies upon its face, and all the holy angels with him praying for him and saying, "Forgive him, Father of all, for he is your image." What then, my child Seth, will this be? And when will he be handed over into the hands of the invisible Father and our God? And who are the two Ethiopians standing by at the prayer of your father?'

Seth said to his mother, 'These are the sun and the moon, and they are falling down and praying on behalf of my father Adam.' Eve said to him, 'And where is their light, and why have they become black in appearance?' And Seth said to her, 'They cannot shine before the Light of all things, and for this reason the light has been hidden from them.'

While Seth was speaking to his mother, the angels lying on their faces sounded their trumpets and cried out with a fearful voice, saying, 'Blessed is the glory of the Lord over his creations, for he has had mercy on Adam, the work of his hands.' When the angels cried this out, one of the six-winged Seraphim came and took Adam away to the Acherusian Lake and washed him before God. And he spent three hours lying there, and then the Master of all, sitting on his holy throne, stretched out his hands, took Adam, and handed him over to the archangel Michael, saying to him, 'Take him into Paradise, as far as the third heaven, and leave him there until that great and fearful day which I am about to ordain for the world.' And Michael the archangel, taking Adam, led him away and left him, just as God had told him concerning the pardon of Adam.

After all these things, then, the archangel made request concerning the burial of the body. And God commanded that all the angels assemble before him, each according to his rank. And all the angels gathered together, some holding censers and others trumpets. And the Lord of hosts mounted up, and the winds drew him, and Cherubim mounted upon the winds, and the angels of heaven went before him. And having come to where the body of Adam was, they took it. And they came into Paradise, and all the plants of Paradise were shaken, so that all those born of Adam became drowsy from the fragrance, except for Seth, because he had been born according to the decree of God.

The body of Adam was lying, then, upon the earth in Paradise, and Seth grieved exceedingly over him. And the Lord God said, 'Adam, why did you do this? If you had kept my commandment, those who brought you down to this place would not be rejoicing. Nevertheless, I tell you that I will turn their joy into sorrow, but your sorrow I will turn into joy; and returning, I will establish you in your dominion upon the throne of the one who deceived you, and he shall be cast into this place, so that you may sit above him. Then he and those who listened to him shall be condemned, and they will grieve greatly and weep when they see you sitting upon his honorable throne.'

And then he spoke to the archangel Michael, 'Go away into Paradise in the third heaven and bring me three linen cloths of fine linen and silk.' And God said to Michael, Gabriel, Uriel, and Raphael, 'Cover the body of Adam with the linen cloths, and bring oil from the oil of fragrance and pour it over him.' And having done so, they prepared his body for burial. And the Lord spoke, 'Let the body of Abel also be brought.' And bringing other linen cloths, they prepared him also for burial, since he had remained unburied from the day that Cain his brother murdered him. For although wicked Cain took great pains to hide it, he was not able, for the earth would not receive it, saying, 'I will not receive another body until the dust taken from me and formed comes to me.' Then angels took it and placed it upon a rock until his father died, and both were buried according to the command of God in the regions of Paradise, in the place where God found the dust. And God sent seven angels into Paradise, and they brought many sweet spices and placed them in the earth; and so they took the two bodies and buried them in the place which they had dug and constructed.

Then God called Adam and said, 'Adam, Adam!' And the body answered from the earth and said, 'Here I am, Lord.' And the Lord said to him, 'I told you that you are dust, and to dust you shall return. Again I promise you the resurrection: I will raise you up on the last day in the resurrection with every person from your seed.'

After these words, God made a three-cornered seal and sealed the tomb, so that no one might do anything to him during the six days until his rib should be returned to him. And when the loving God and the holy angels had departed to their place, after the six days Eve also died. While she was still alive, she wept about her death because she did not know where her body was to be laid. For when the Lord was present in Paradise at the burial of Adam, she and her children were asleep, except Seth, as I said. And Eve prayed at the hour of her death that she might be buried where Adam her husband was, saying thus: 'My Master, Lord, and God of all power, do not alienate me, your handmaid, from the body of Adam, for you made me from his members; but deem me worthy, even me, the unworthy and sinful one, to be buried together by his body. Just as I was with him in Paradise and inseparable even after the transgression, so let no one separate us.' Then after praying, she looked up to heaven, stood up, beat her breast, and said, 'God of all, receive my spirit.' And immediately she yielded up her spirit to God.

When she died, the archangel Michael arrived, and three angels having come, they took her body and buried it where the body of Abel was. And the archangel Michael said to Seth, 'Thus shall you bury every person who dies until the day of resurrection.' And after giving this law, he said to him, 'Do not mourn beyond six days; but on the seventh day rest and rejoice on it, because on it God and we angels rejoice over a righteous soul that has departed from the earth.' Having said these things, the archangel Michael went up into heaven, glorifying and saying, 'Hallelujah, Holy, Holy, Holy is the Lord,' to the glory of God the Father, because to him belong glory, honor, and worship, with his unoriginate and life-giving Spirit, now and always and unto the ages of ages. Amen.

unit.reading: When they were driven out from paradise, they made a hut for themselves and spent seven days weeping and mourning in great sorrow. But after seven days they began to hunger and sought food to eat, but they found none.

Then Eve said to Adam: "My lord, I am hungry. Go, search for something for us to eat. Perhaps the Lord God will look upon us and have mercy on us and call us back to the place where we were before." And Adam arose and walked seven days throughout all that land, but did not find food such as they had in paradise.

And Eve said to Adam: "My lord, do you think—would that you might cause me to die! And perhaps the Lord God will bring you back again into paradise, since on my account the Lord God is angry with you. Do you wish to kill me so that I may die? And perhaps the Lord God will bring you into paradise, because on my account you were driven out from there." Adam answered: "Do not speak such things, Eve, lest the Lord God bring some further curse upon us again. How can it be that I should put forth my hand against my own flesh? But let us arise and seek for ourselves that by which we may live, so that we do not perish."

And as they walked, they searched for nine days, and they did not find anything such as they had in paradise; rather, they found only what the animals ate. And Adam said to Eve: "The Lord gave these things to the animals and beasts to eat, but ours was angelic food. Yet justly and deservedly do we lament before the presence of God who made us. Let us repent with a great repentance; perhaps the Lord God will show forbearance and have mercy upon us, and provide for us that by which we may live."

And Eve said to Adam: "My lord, tell me, what is repentance and how should I repent, lest perhaps we impose upon ourselves a toil which we cannot bear, and the Lord not hear our prayers and turn his face away from us, because we did not fulfill what we promised. My lord, how much do you intend to repent, since it is I who brought toil and tribulation upon you?"

And Adam said to Eve: "You cannot do as much as I, but do only as much as will save you. For I will spend forty days fasting; but you, arise and go to the river Tigris, and take a stone and stand upon it in the water up to your neck in the depth of the river. And let no word come out of your mouth, because we are unworthy to entreat the Lord, since our lips are unclean from the forbidden and prohibited tree. And stand in the water of the river for thirty-seven days. But I will spend forty days in the water of the Jordan. Perhaps the Lord God will have mercy upon us."
And Eve went to the river Tigris and did as Adam told her. Likewise, Adam went to the river Jordan and stood upon a stone up to his neck in the water.

And Adam said: "I say to you, water of the Jordan, grieve with me and gather to me all swimming creatures that are in you, and let them surround me and mourn together with me. Let them not weep for themselves, but for me, because they did not sin, but I did." Immediately all living creatures came and surrounded him, and the water of the Jordan stood still from that hour, ceasing its flow.

And eighteen days passed. Then Satan grew angry and transformed himself into the brightness of angels, and went to the river Tigris to Eve and found her weeping. And the devil himself, as if grieving with her, began to weep and said to her: "Come out of the river and weep no longer. Now cease from your sorrow and groaning. Why are you and your husband Adam anxious? The Lord God has heard your groaning and accepted your repentance; and all we angels have pleaded for you, entreating the Lord, and he sent me to bring you out of the water and give you the nourishment that you had in paradise and for which you have wept. Now therefore come out of the water, and I will lead you to the place where your food is prepared."

Hearing these things, Eve believed and came out of the water of the river, and her flesh was like grass from the cold of the water. And when she had come out, she fell to the ground, and the devil lifted her up and led her to Adam. But when Adam saw her and the devil with her, he cried out with weeping, saying: "O Eve, O Eve, where is the work of your repentance? How have you been seduced again by our adversary, through whom we have been estranged from the dwelling of paradise and from spiritual joy?"

When Eve heard this, she recognized that the devil had persuaded her to leave the river, and she fell on her face to the earth, and her grief and groaning and lamentation were doubled. And she cried out, saying: "Woe to you, devil! Why do you attack us for no reason? What have you to do with us? Or what have we done to you, that you pursue us deceitfully? Or how does your malice concern us? Did we take away your glory and cause you to be without honor? Why do you pursue us, enemy, unto death, impiously and enviously?"

And groaning, the devil said: "O Adam, all my enmity and envy and grief are directed against you, because on your account I was cast out and alienated from my glory, which I had in the heavens in the midst of the angels, and on your account I was hurled down to the earth." Adam answered: "What have I done to you, or what is my fault against you? Since you were neither harmed nor injured by us, why do you pursue us?"

The devil answered: "Adam, what are you saying to me? On your account I was cast out from there. When you were formed, I was cast out from the face of God and sent away from the fellowship of the angels. When God breathed the breath of life into you, and your face and likeness were made according to the image of God, Michael brought you and made you be worshiped in the presence of God; and the Lord God said: 'Behold Adam, I have made you in our image and likeness.'"

And Michael went out and called all the angels, saying: 'Worship the image of the Lord God, as the Lord God has commanded.' And Michael himself was the first to worship, and he called me and said: 'Worship the image of the Lord God.' And I answered: 'I have no need to worship Adam.' And when Michael compelled me to worship, I said to him: 'Why do you compel me? I will not worship one inferior and posterior to me. In his creation I am prior; before he was made, I had already been made. He ought to worship me.'"

Hearing this, the other angels who were under me refused to worship him. And Michael said: 'Worship the image of God; but if you do not worship, the Lord God will be angry with you.' And I said: 'If he is angry with me, I will set my seat above the stars of heaven and I will be like the Most High.'"

And the Lord God was angry with me and sent me with my angels out from our glory, and on your account we were cast out from our dwellings into this world and hurled to the earth. And immediately we were plunged into sorrow, because we were stripped of so great glory. And we grieved to see you in such joy of delights. And with deceit I circumvented your wife and caused you to be cast out through her from the delights of your joy, just as I was cast out from my glory."

Hearing these things from the devil, Adam cried out with great weeping and said: "O Lord my God, in your hands is my life. Cause this adversary of mine to be far from me, who seeks to destroy my life, and give me his glory, which he himself lost." And immediately the devil vanished from his sight. But Adam persevered for forty days standing in repentance in the water of the Jordan.

And Eve said to Adam: "May you live, my lord. Life has been granted to you, because you committed neither the first nor the second transgression, but I transgressed and was deceived, because I did not keep the commandment of God. And now separate me from the light of this life, and I will go toward the setting of the sun and will be there until I die." And she began to walk toward the western regions and began to mourn and weep bitterly with great groaning. And she made a dwelling place there, having in her womb an offspring of three months.

And when the time of her delivery drew near, she began to be tormented with pains, and she cried out to the Lord, saying: "Have mercy on me, Lord; help me!" But she was not heard, nor was the mercy of God around her. And she said to herself: "Who will announce this to my lord Adam? I beseech you, luminaries of heaven, when you return to the east, bring word to my lord Adam."

In that hour Adam said: "The wailing of Eve has reached me; perhaps the serpent has fought with her again." And going, he found her in great distress; and Eve said: "From the moment I saw you, my lord, my soul set in pains has found relief. And now pray to the Lord God for me, that he may hear you and look upon me and deliver me from my terrible pains." And Adam prayed to the Lord for Eve.

And behold, twelve angels and two powers came, standing on the right and on the left of Eve. And Michael was standing on the right, and he touched her face down to her breast and said to Eve: "Blessed are you, Eve, on account of Adam. Because his prayers and supplications are great, I have been sent to you so that you may receive our help. Arise now and prepare yourself for giving birth." And she gave birth to a son, and he was radiant. And immediately the infant arose, ran, and took grass in his hands and gave it to his mother. And his name was called Cain.

And Adam took Eve and the boy and led them to the east. And the Lord God sent various seeds through the angel Michael and gave them to Adam, and showed him how to labor and cultivate the ground, so that they might have fruit by which they and all their generations might live.

Afterward Eve conceived and bore a son whose name was Abel. And Cain and Abel stayed together. And Eve said to Adam: "My lord, while sleeping I saw a vision, as it were the blood of our son Abel in the hand of Cain, who was swallowing it with his mouth. On this account I am in grief." And Adam said: "Woe, lest Cain kill Abel! But let us separate them from each other and make separate dwellings for them." And they made Cain a tiller of the soil and made Abel a shepherd, so that they might be separated from each other in this way. And after this Cain killed Abel. Adam was then one hundred and thirty years old; and Abel was killed when he was one hundred and twenty-two years old.

And after this Adam knew his wife, and she bore a son, and he called his name Seth. And Adam said to Eve: "Behold, I have fathered a son in place of Abel, whom Cain killed." And after Adam fathered Seth, he lived eight hundred years and fathered thirty sons and thirty daughters, in all sixty-three children. And they multiplied upon the earth in their nations.

And Adam said to Seth: "Listen, my son Seth, that I may tell you the things I heard and saw. After I and your mother were cast out of paradise, while we were in prayer, the archangel Michael, the messenger of God, came to me. And I saw a chariot like the wind, and its wheels were of fire, and I was caught up into the paradise of righteousness. And I saw the Lord sitting, and his appearance was an intolerable, burning fire. And many thousands of angels were on the right and on the left of that chariot.

Seeing these things, I was troubled and fear seized me, and I worshiped before God upon the face of the earth. And God said to me: 'Behold, you shall die, because you have transgressed the commandment of God, because you listened more to the voice of your wife, whom I gave into your authority so that you might have her under your will; and you listened to her and transgressed my words.'

And when I heard these words of God, falling down to the earth I worshiped the Lord and said: 'My Lord, Almighty God, merciful, holy, and gracious, let not the name of the memory of your majesty be blotted out! But restore my soul, for I am dying and my spirit will depart from my mouth. Do not cast me away from your face, whom you formed from the dust of the earth, nor set aside from your grace him whom you nurtured.' And behold, his word came to me, and the Lord said to me: 'Because your days are numbered, you have become a lover of knowledge; on this account there shall not be taken away from your seed forever one to minister before me.'

And when I heard these words, I prostrated myself on the earth and worshiped the Lord God, saying: 'You are the eternal and most high God, and all creatures give you honor and praise. You are the true light shining above all light, the living life, the power of incomprehensible greatness. The spiritual hosts give you honor and praise. You perform with humankind the great deeds of your mercy.'

After I had worshiped the Lord, immediately Michael, the archangel of God, took hold of my hand and led me out from the paradise of the visitation and command of God. And Michael, holding a rod in his hand, touched the waters that were around paradise, and they froze. And I crossed over, and Michael crossed over with me and brought me back to the place from which he had caught me up. Listen, my son Seth, also to the rest of the mysteries and future secrets that were revealed to me, which by eating from the tree of knowledge I came to know and understand, concerning what will happen in this age:

... the future things that will be in this temporal age, which God will do for his creature, humankind. The Lord will appear in a flame of fire. From the mouth of his majesty he will give commandments and precepts to all (from his mouth will proceed a sword sharp on both sides), and they will sanctify him in the house of the habitation of his majesty. And he will show them the wondrous place of his majesty.

And then they will build a house to the Lord their God in the land which he provided for them (which he will prepare for them), and there they will transgress his commandments, and their sanctuary will be burned, and their land will be deserted, and they themselves will be dispersed because they provoked God to anger. And again (on the third, seventh day) he will save them from their dispersion, and they will build the house of God again, and at the last the house of God will be exalted greater than before. And again iniquity will surpass righteousness.

And after this, God will dwell with humans on earth, visible to sight. And then righteousness will begin to shine, and the house of God will be honored forever, and adversities will no longer be able to harm those who believe in God. And God will raise up for himself a faithful people, whom he will save forever and ever. And the ungodly who refuse to love his law will be punished by God their king. Heaven and earth, night and day, and all creatures will obey him, and will not transgress his commandment nor alter their works. But humans will be changed, abandoning the law of the Lord.

Because of this, the Lord will cast away the ungodly from himself, and the righteous will shine like the sun in the presence of God. And at that time humans will be purified by water from sins. But those who refuse to be purified by water will be condemned. And blessed will be the person who has set right their soul when the judgments and wondrous deeds of God occur among humans, and their deeds are examined by God, the righteous judge.

When Adam had reached nine hundred and thirty years, knowing that his days were drawing to a close, he said: "Let all my children gather to me, that I may bless them before I die and speak with them." And they gathered into three parts before his presence, in front of the place of prayer where they worshiped the Lord God. And they asked him: "What is the matter with you, father, that you have gathered us? And why are you lying in your bed?" And answering, Adam said: "My children, I am ill with pains." And all his children said to him: "Father, what does it mean to be ill with pains?"

Then his son Seth said: "Lord, have you perhaps longed for the fruit of paradise, from which you used to eat, and on that account you lie sorrowful? Tell me, and I will go to the nearest gates of paradise and put dust on my head and cast myself on the earth before the gates of paradise and weep in great lamentation, entreating the Lord. Perhaps he will hear me and send his angel to bring me some of the fruit that you have desired." Adam answered and said: "No, my son, I do not long for it, but I have weakness and great pain in my body." Seth answered: "What is pain, my lord father? I do not know; do not hide it from us, but tell us."

And Adam answered and said, "Hear me, my children. When God made us, me and your mother, and placed us in Paradise and gave us every fruit-bearing tree to eat, he forbade us: 'Do not eat from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, which is in the midst of Paradise.' God also assigned portions of Paradise to me and to your mother: to me he gave the trees of the eastern and northern parts, which face the north wind, and to your mother he gave the southern and western parts."

The Lord God gave us two angels to guard us. The hour came when the angels ascended before God to worship. Immediately, the adversary, the devil, found an opportunity while the angels were absent. And the devil seduced your mother so that she ate from the forbidden and prohibited tree; and she ate and gave to me.

And immediately the Lord God grew angry with us, and the Lord said to me, "Because you have abandoned my commandment and have not kept my word which I enjoined upon you, behold, I will bring seventy plagues upon your body; you shall be tormented with various pains from the crown of your head and eyes and ears down to the nails of your feet and through each individual limb." These things he appointed for chastisement ... together with the trees. Now all these things the Lord has sent upon me and upon all our generations.

Saying these things to all his children, Adam was seized with great pains, and crying out with loud shouts he said, "What shall I do, wretched as I am, placed in such pains?" And when Eve saw him weeping, she herself began to weep, saying, "Lord my God, transfer his pain onto me, for it is I who sinned." And Eve said to Adam, "My lord, give me a portion of your pains, for this guilt came upon you through me."

And Adam said to Eve, "Arise and go with my son Seth to the vicinity of Paradise, and put dust upon your heads, and prostrate yourselves upon the ground, and mourn before God. Perhaps he will have mercy and send his angel to the tree of his mercy, from which flows the oil of life, and give you a little of it, so that you may anoint me with it, that I may find rest from these pains by which I am consumed."

And Seth and his mother went toward the gates of Paradise; and while they were walking, behold, suddenly a beast, a serpent, came and made an attack and bit Seth. And when Eve saw it, she wept, saying, "Woe to me, wretched one, for I am cursed, because I did not keep the commandments of the Lord!" And Eve said to the serpent with a loud voice, "Accursed beast, how were you not afraid to throw yourself against the image of God, but dared to fight against it? Or how did your teeth prevail?"

The beast answered with a human voice, "O Eve, is not our malice directed at you? Is not our fury against you? Tell me, Eve, how was your mouth opened so that you ate of the fruit which the Lord God commanded you not to eat? And now can you not bear it if I begin to reproach you?"

Then Seth said to the beast, "May the Lord God rebuke you! Be silenced, be dumb! Shut your mouth, accursed enemy of truth, confusion of perdition! Depart from the image of God until the day when the Lord God shall order you to be brought to trial." And the beast said to Seth, "Behold, I depart, as you have said, from the presence of the image of God." Immediately the wound from the teeth departed from Seth.

Then Seth and his mother walked toward the regions of Paradise for the sake of the oil of mercy, that they might anoint the ailing Adam. And arriving at the gates of Paradise, they took dust from the earth and placed it upon their heads. And they prostrated themselves upon the earth on their faces and began to weep with great groaning, entreating the Lord God to have mercy on Adam in his pains and to send his angel to give them oil from the tree of his mercy.

While they were praying and entreating for many hours, behold, the angel Michael, appearing to them, said, "I have been sent to you by the Lord; I have been appointed by the Lord over the human body. I say to you, Seth, man of God: do not weep with praying and supplication for the oil of the tree of mercy to anoint your father Adam because of the pains of his body."

"For I tell you that in no way will you be able to receive any of it, except in the last days, when five thousand and five hundred years are completed. Then the most beloved King, Christ the Son of God, will come upon the earth to raise up the body of Adam, and with him to raise up the bodies of the dead. And the Son of God himself, when he comes, will be baptized in the river Jordan; and when he has come out of the water of the Jordan, he will then anoint all who believe in him with the oil of his mercy. And the oil of mercy shall be from generation to generation for those who are to be born anew from water and the Holy Spirit into eternal life. Then descending upon the earth, the most beloved Son of God, Christ, will lead your father Adam into Paradise to the tree of mercy."

"You, however, Seth, go to your father Adam, for the time of his life is completed. In six more days his soul will depart from his body; and when it departs, you will see great wonders in heaven and on earth and in the heavenly luminaries." Saying these things, Michael immediately departed from Seth. And Eve and Seth returned, and they brought with them sweet spices, that is, nard, saffron, calamint, and cinnamon.

And when Seth and his mother arrived at Adam, they told him that the serpent-beast had bitten Seth. And Adam said to Eve, "What have you done? You have brought upon us a great blow, transgression and sin upon our entire generation! And this which you have done will be recounted to your children after my death, for those who shall arise from us, toiling, will not have enough but will fail and curse us, saying: 'Our parents, who were from the beginning, have brought all evils upon us!'" Hearing these things, Eve began to weep and groan.

And just as Michael the archangel foretold, after six days Adam's death came. When Adam knew that the hour of his death had arrived, he said to all his children, "Behold, I am nine hundred and thirty years old; and when I die, bury me opposite the east of God's great dwelling place." And it came to pass, when he had finished all his words, he gave up the spirit.

The sun, moon, and stars were darkened for seven days. And while Seth was embracing his father's body, mourning over it, and Eve was looking down at the earth with her hands clasped over her head and resting her head upon her knees, and all his children were weeping with most bitter tears, behold, the angel Michael appeared, standing at Adam's head, and said to Seth, "Arise from above the body of your father, come to me, and see what the Lord God ordains concerning him. He is his creation, and he has had mercy on him."

And all the angels, sounding trumpets, said, "Blessed are you, Lord, for you have had mercy on your creation." Then Seth saw the outstretched hand of the Lord holding Adam; and he delivered him to Michael, saying, "Let him be in your custody until the day of dispensation in punishments until the last years, when I shall turn his mourning into joy. Then he shall sit upon the throne of him who supplanted him."

And the Lord said again to the angels Michael and Uriel, "Bring me three linen shrouds of fine byssus and spread them over Adam, and other shrouds over Abel his son, and bury Adam and his son." And all the angelic hosts marched before Adam, and the sleep of the dead was sanctified. And the angels Michael and Uriel buried Adam and Abel in the regions of Paradise, with Seth and his mother watching, and no one else. And Michael and Uriel said, "Just as you have seen, in like manner bury your dead."

Six days after Adam died, Eve, knowing her own death was near, gathered all her sons and her daughters—who were Seth with thirty brothers and thirty sisters—and Eve said to all of them, "Hear me, my children, that I may tell you how I and your father transgressed the commandment of God; and the archangel Michael said to us: 'Because of your transgressions, our Lord will bring upon your race the wrath of his judgment: first by water, secondly by fire. By these two the Lord will judge the entire human race.'"

"So hear me, my children! Make stone tablets and other tablets of clay, and write on them the whole life of me and of your father, what you have heard and seen from us. If he judges our race by water, the clay tablets will dissolve and the stone tablets will endure. But if he judges our race by fire, the stone tablets will break down and the clay ones from earth will be baked hard." When Eve had said all these things to her children, she stretched out her hands toward heaven, praying and bending her knees to the earth, and worshiping the Lord and giving thanks, she gave up the spirit.

Afterward, with great weeping, all her children buried her. When they had been mourning for four days, the archangel Michael then appeared to them, saying to Seth, "Man of God, do not mourn your dead for more than six days, because the seventh day is a sign of the resurrection, the rest of the age to come; and on the seventh day the Lord rested from all his works." Then Seth made the tablets.

Then Seth made two tablets of stone and two of clay, and formed the strokes of letters, and wrote upon them the life of his father Adam and of his mother Eve, which he had heard from them and seen with his own eyes; and he placed the tablets in the midst of his father's house, in the place of prayer where he used to pray to the Lord. And after the deluge, those inscribed tablets were seen by many people, but they could be read by no one.

Now Solomon the wise saw the writing and prayed to the Lord, and an angel of the Lord appeared to him, saying, "I am the one who held the hand of Seth so that he might write upon these stones with his finger. And you shall be knowledgeable of the writing, so that you may recognize and understand what all these stones contain, and where the place of prayer was in which Adam and Eve used to worship the Lord God. And you must build there the temple of the Lord, that is, the house of prayer."
Then Solomon completed the temple of the Lord God and called those letters 'Achiliac,' that is, written without instruction in words, by the finger of Seth while the angel of the Lord held his hand.

And on those very stones was found what Enoch, the seventh from Adam, prophesied before the flood concerning the coming of Christ, saying: "Behold, the Lord shall come among his holy ones to execute judgment upon all, and to convict the ungodly of all their deeds about which sinners and ungodly grumblers and irreligious people have spoken against him, who walk according to their own desires, and whose mouth has spoken pride."
