unit.reading: Concerning the expulsion of Adam and Eve from paradise.

It came to pass, when Adam and his wife Eve were expelled from paradise, departing they went to the west and made for themselves a tent, and they were there six days mourning and crying out in great tribulation. And after six days they began to hunger; they sought to eat and found nothing to eat;

Eve said to Adam, “My lord, I am very hungry; why do you not go and seek something for us to eat, so that we may see whether the Lord God will perhaps have mercy on us and recall us to the place where we were before?” And Adam arose after eight days and walked through all that land, and he did not find food such as they had at first.

Eve said again to Adam, “My lord, I am dying of hunger; would that I might die, and perhaps be killed by you, because on account of me the Lord God is angry with you.” And Adam said, “Great is his creation in heaven and on earth; whether on account of you or on account of me, I do not know.” And Eve said again to Adam, “My lord, kill me so that I may die and be removed from the face of the Lord God and from the sight of his angels, that the Lord God may forget his anger toward you, so that perhaps he may bring you into paradise, since on my account you were expelled from it.” And Adam said, “Do not speak such things, Eve, lest the Lord God bring a curse upon us again. How can it be that I should lay my hand upon my own flesh? But arise, let us go and seek something by which we may live and not perish.”

Going out, they sought and found nothing such as they had in paradise; yet they found that which the animals and beasts were eating. And Adam said, “God has given these things to the animals and beasts for living.” And Adam said again, “Let us mourn before the Lord God who made us, and let us repent in great penance for forty days, if perhaps the Lord God may forgive us and provide for us whereby we may live.”

And Eve said to Adam, “My lord, what is penance, or in what manner shall we repent, lest perhaps we impose on ourselves that which we cannot fulfill, and our prayers not be heard and God turn his face away from us, if we do not fulfill what we have promised?”

And Adam said, “Can you not do as many, and will you not do so? I say to you, do as many as you wish; for I will do forty-seven days, because on the seventh day I was made and on the seventh day God finished all things.” And he said to Eve, “Arise and go to the river Tigris, and take a stone with you, and stand upon it in the water up to your neck, and let no word proceed from your mouth, because we are unworthy to entreat the Lord, since our lips are unclean because we ate from the forbidden tree. Remain there for forty days, and I in the Jordan for forty-seven days, if perhaps the Lord God will have mercy on us.”

And she went to the river Tigris just as Adam said, and he came to the river Jordan, having a stone with him, and stood in the river up to his neck, and the hair of their heads was spread out over the waters.

Then Adam said, “I say to you, Jordan, grieve with me, and gather all the living creatures that are within you, and surround me and mourn with me; do not mourn on your own account, but on mine, because you yourselves have not sinned, but I have already sinned wickedly against the Lord; neither have you committed an offense, nor have you been deprived of your sustenance, but I have sinned and have been deprived of the food granted to me.” When Adam said these things, behold, all the living creatures came and surrounded him, and the water of the river stood still in that hour. Then Adam cried out to the Lord God, and his throat grew hoarse day by day; and nineteen days passed that all the living creatures were mourning with Adam.

Then their adversary Satan was troubled, and transforming himself into the brightness of an angel, he went away to the river Tigris where Eve was. And when he saw her weeping with great sorrow, he himself also began to weep. Afterward he said to her, “Come out, return and rest, and weep no more; now cease from your sorrow about which you are anxious; for the Lord has heard your groaning and accepted your penance, wherefore we and all the angels have pleaded with him through your affliction, and he has sent me to lead you out of the water and to give you your sustenance which you had and lost because of your sin. Now therefore come out, and I will lead you to your place where your food is prepared.”

And then Eve came out of the water, and her flesh was green like grass from the coldness of the water. But while she was walking, she fell to the ground and lay as if dead for almost the whole day. And the devil lifted her up from the ground; and she went to Adam, and the devil with her. Seeing them, Adam cried out with weeping, saying, “O Eve, where is the work of your penance? How have you been deceived by your adversary, through whom we have been alienated from the habitation of paradise and spiritual joy?”

When Eve heard these things, she recognized that the devil had deceived her and persuaded her to come out of the river; and she fell upon the face of the earth, and her grief and groaning and lamentation were doubled. But Adam cried out, saying, “Woe to you, devil, who do not cease to attack us so severely! What have we to do with you? What have we done to you that you persecute us so deceitfully? Or what is your malice to us? Have we taken away your glory, or made you to be without honor? Are we your enemies unto death, ungodly and envious one?”

Groaning, the devil said to him, “O Adam, all the enmity and envy and grief are from you, because on account of you I was cast out from my glory and alienated from the brightness that I had in the midst of the angels, and on account of you I was cast down to the earth.” And Adam answered, “What have I done to you, or what is my fault, when I did not know you?”

The devil answered, “What is this that you say, that you have done nothing? Yet for your sake I was cast down. On the day when you were formed, I was cast down from the face of God and sent outside the fellowship of the angels, when God breathed the breath of life into you, and your countenance and your likeness were made in the image of God; and Michael brought you and made you be worshiped in the presence of God, and God said, ‘Behold, I have made Adam in your image and likeness,’

and going out, Michael called all the angels and said, ‘Worship the image of the Lord God, just as the Lord commanded.’ And Michael was the first to worship you, and he called me and said to me, ‘Worship the image of the Lord God.’ And I answered, ‘No, I do not have to worship Adam.’ And when Michael compelled me to worship, I said to him, ‘Why do you compel me? I will not worship one inferior to me, because I am prior before every creature, and before he was made I had already been made; he ought to worship me, not I him.’

Hearing these things, the other angels who are with me were unwilling to worship; and Michael said to me, ‘Worship the image of God; but if you do not worship, the Lord God will be angry with you.’ And I said, ‘If he is angry with me, I will set my throne above the stars of heaven, and I will be like the Most High.’

And the Lord God was angry with me, and commanded me with my angels to be cast out from heaven and from my glory. And thus on account of you we were expelled from our habitations and cast down to the earth. And immediately I was in grief because I was stripped of all my glory, and you were placed in delights and joy. Therefore I began to envy you and could not endure that you should glory in such a way. I deceived your wife, and through her I caused you to be expelled from all your delights and joys, just as I was first expelled.”

Hearing these things, Adam cried out with great weeping and said, “Lord God, my life is in your hands; make this adversary be far from me, who seeks to destroy my soul. Give me, Lord, the glory from which he was cast down.” And the devil vanished from his eyes. But Adam persevered in penance for forty-seven days in the water of the Jordan.

And Eve said to Adam, “As my lord lives, life is granted to you, because you did not transgress either the first time or the second, but I have transgressed and was deceived because I did not keep the commandments of God. And now separate me from the light of this life, and I will go to the setting of the sun and will be there until I die.” And she began to walk toward the regions of the west, and she began to mourn and to weep bitterly with great groaning; and she made for herself a dwelling, having conceived in her womb a child of three months.

Now when the time of her giving birth drew near, she began to be troubled with pains, and cried out to the Lord, saying, “Have mercy on me, Lord, and help me.” And she was not heard, nor was there anyone who might help her; and she said within herself, “Who will announce these things to my lord? I beseech you, luminaries of heaven, when you return to the east, announce to my lord Adam.” And so it was done.

And Adam said, “The weeping of Eve has come to me; lest perhaps the serpent should fight with her again, I will go visit her.” And walking, he found her mourning in great grief. Seeing him, Eve said, “Ever since my lord saw me, my soul placed in sorrow has been refreshed. But now pray to the Lord for me, that he may help and deliver me from my terrible pains.” And Adam prayed to the Lord for her.

And behold, twelve angels and two virtues came, standing at the right and left of Eve; and Michael, standing at her right, touched her face down to her breast, and the angel said, “Blessed are you, Eve, on account of Adam, because his prayers are great; at his supplication I have been sent to you that you may receive help from the angels of God. Arise and prepare yourself for giving birth.” And she prepared herself and gave birth to a son, and he was shining. And immediately the infant arose, ran, and taking grass in his hands, gave it to his mother. And his name was called Cain.

And Adam, taking Eve with the child, led them to the east. And the Lord sent Michael to teach Adam to work the earth and to gather fruit, by which they themselves and all generations after him might be able to live.

Eve conceived again and bore a son, and they called his name Abel. And Cain dwelt together with Abel. And Eve said to Adam, “My lord, while sleeping I saw in a vision that Cain was conveying the blood of your son Abel in his hands, and swallowed it with his mouth.” And Adam said, “Perhaps he will kill him. But let us separate them from one another, and make for them separate dwellings.” And they made Cain a farmer and Abel a shepherd, and thus they were separated from one another. Afterward, however, Cain killed his brother Abel. Now Adam was then one hundred and thirty years old. Abel, however, was killed by Cain in the one hundred and second year of his age.

Afterward Adam knew his wife Eve, and he fathered a son by her and called his name Seth; and Adam said, “Behold, I have fathered a son in place of Abel, whom Cain killed.” And Adam lived eight hundred years after he fathered Seth, and he fathered thirty sons and thirty-two daughters, who were multiplied upon the earth in their nations.

And Adam said to his son Seth, “Hear, my son, what I shall tell you. After I and your mother were cast out of paradise naked, when we were in prayer, Michael the archangel, the messenger of God, came to me, and I saw chariots like winds and his wheel was fiery, and I was caught up into the paradise of righteousness, and I saw the Lord, and his appearance was intolerable, burning with rays; and a multitude of angels preceded the rays, and many other wondrous things of angels were on the right and on the left,

and the Lord said to me, ‘Behold, you shall die because you transgressed my commandment and listened to the voice of your wife, whom I gave into your power that you might have her according to your will, and you obeyed her and not me.’

And when I heard these words of God, falling to the earth I prayed to the Lord and said, ‘O most omnipotent and most merciful God, holy and gracious, let not the memory of the name of your majesty be blotted out, but convert my soul, for I am dying and my spirit is going out of my mouth; do not cast me away from your face, whom you formed from the dust of the earth; do not disregard him whom your grace has nourished; behold, your word consumes me.’ And the Lord said, ‘Because the disposition of your heart has been made to love knowledge, on account of this it shall not be taken from your seed forever to minister to me.’

And when I had heard these words of the Lord, I prostrated myself on the earth and worshiped the Lord, saying, ‘You are the eternal and supreme God, and every creature of yours gives you honor and praise. You are above all shining light, true and incomprehensible light of life; O greatness of the power of the living God, every living creature gives you spiritual honor and praise, since you made humankind with great power.’

And after I prayed these things, immediately Michael, the archangel of God, took hold of my hand and cast me out from the midst of the paradise of the visitation and vision of God. And Michael, holding a rod in his hand, touched the waters that were around paradise, and the waters froze, and I crossed over them, and Michael crossed with me and brought me back to the place of paradise from where he had taken me. And Adam said again, ‘Hear, my son Seth, the remaining mysteries and future sacraments revealed to me; for through the tree of knowledge of which I ate, I recognized and understood the things that will happen in this temporal age, what God will do concerning humankind. God will appear in a flame of fire from the mouth of his majesty, and will give commandments and precepts to all, and will sanctify him in the house of his majesty; and God will show them the wondrous place of his majesty, and there they will transgress his precepts, and their sanctuary will be burned, and their lands will be deserted, and they will be scattered because they provoked God. On the seventh day he will save them again from their dispersion, and they will build a house again for their God on the earth, and the latter house of God will be preserved more than the former; and again iniquity will overcome righteousness, and afterward God will dwell with humans visibly on earth, and righteousness will begin to shine, and the house of God will be honored by angels, and the adversary will not be able to harm the humans who believe in God. And God will raise up a people for himself, to make them saved forever and ever. And the righteous will place Adam in his kingdom, and those who wished to love his kingdom, heaven and earth, day and night they will worship, and all creatures will obey the Lord, and will not transgress his precepts, nor will their works be changed. But humans will be changed, abandoning the precepts of the Lord. After this the Lord will cast away the ungodly, and the righteous will endure like righteousness before God; and at that time they will be purified from sins, but following those unwilling to be purified by water; and happy is every person who corrects his soul, because the day of great judgment will be among mortals, and their deeds will be examined by God, the righteous judge.’

And after Adam reached nine hundred and thirty years, knowing that the days of his life were ending, he said to Eve, “Let all my sons and my daughters be gathered before me so that I may speak with them and bless them before I die.” And they assembled in three groups before their father’s presence, in front of the place of prayer where Adam used to pray to the Lord God. And all gathered together said with one voice, “What is the matter with you, father, that you have gathered us, and why do you lie on your bed?” Adam answered and said, “My children, I am ill and tormented with pains.” And his children said to him, “Father, what does it mean to be ill and to be tormented with pains?”

And his son Seth said, “Lord father, perhaps you have desired to eat of the fruit of paradise of which you once ate, and therefore you lie grieving. Tell me if you wish that I should go near the gates of paradise, and put dust upon my head and throw myself on the ground before the gates of paradise and weep with great lamentation, praying to the Lord God; and perhaps he will hear me and send his angel to bring me some of the fruit that you desire.” Adam answered and said, “Son, I do not desire it, but I am weak and have great pains in my body.” Seth answered, “I do not know what pain is; do you not wish to tell us? Why do you hide it from us?”

And Adam said, “Hear me, all my sons and my daughters. When the Lord God made me and your mother and placed us in paradise, he gave us every fruit-bearing tree to eat, and told us not to eat from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, which is in the midst of paradise. Now the Lord had placed us in paradise and gave me dominion over the east and the part that faces the north, and to your mother he gave the south and the western part,

and he gave us two angels to guard us. The hour came for the angels to ascend into the presence of God to worship him. Immediately the devil found an opportunity against your mother and deceived her, and made her eat from the forbidden tree prohibited by God; and she ate and offered it to me, and I immediately ate,

and immediately the Lord God was angry with us in fury, and said to me, ‘Because you have forsaken my commandment and did not keep my word which I appointed for you, behold, I will bring upon your body seventy plagues of diverse pains, from the top of your head, your eyes, and your ears, down to the nails of your feet; and in every limb you and your wife shall be tormented.’ All these things he assigned to us as a scourge of pains along with burnings. Now all these things the Lord has sent upon us and upon all our generation.”

As Adam was saying these things to all his sons, he was seized with great pains, and crying out with loud voices he said, "What shall I do, wretched as I am, placed in such great pains?" And when Eve heard these things, she began to weep and said, "Lord God, transfer his pains to me, because I have sinned." And she said to Adam, "My lord, give me a share of your pains, because through my fault these things have happened."

And Adam said, "Arise, Eve, and go with your son Seth near the gates of Paradise; put dust on your heads and prostrate yourselves and lament before the presence of the Lord God, and perhaps he will have mercy on you and command his angel to be sent to the tree of mercy from which flows the oil of life, and he will give you a little of it so that you may anoint me with it, that I may find rest from these pains by which I am tormented and worn out."

And Seth and his mother Eve went toward the regions of Paradise; and while they were walking, suddenly the serpent, a beast of wickedness, came and bit Seth's face. When Eve saw this, she wept bitterly, saying, "Woe is me, wretched one, for I am cursed, along with all who do not keep the commandments of the Lord God!" And Eve said to the serpent with a loud voice, "O cursed beast, how did you not fear to cast yourself against the image of God? How did you dare to fight with him, or how did your teeth prevail?"

The serpent answered and said with a loud voice, "Is not your wickedness before the Lord? Has he not stirred up our rage against you? Tell me, Eve, how was your mouth opened to eat of the fruit that the Lord commanded you not to eat? Before this, indeed, I had no power over you; but after you transgressed the commandment of the Lord, then our boldness and power against you began."

Then Seth said to the serpent, "May the Lord God rebuke you! Depart from the presence of humans, close your mouth, and be silent, enemy, accursed one, confusion of truth! Depart from the presence of the image of God until the day when the Lord commands you to be brought to trial." And the serpent said to Seth, "Behold, I depart from the face of the image of the Lord God, as you have said." And immediately it departed and left Seth wounded by its teeth.

Then Seth and his mother walked to the gates of Paradise, and they took dust of the earth and put it on their heads, and prostrated themselves upon their faces on the ground, and began to lament with great groaning, beseeching the Lord God to have mercy on Adam who was in pain, and to send his angel to give him oil from the tree of God's mercy.

While they were praying and beseeching with many prayers, behold, the archangel Michael appeared to them, saying, "Seth, what are you seeking? I am the archangel Michael, appointed by the Lord over the bodies of men. I say to you, Seth, man of God: do not weep, praying and beseeching for the oil of the tree of mercy to anoint the body of your father Adam for the pains he suffers in his body.

I say to you that by no means will you be able to have any of it until the last days, when five thousand two hundred and twenty-eight years have been completed. For then Christ, the most beloved Son of God, will come upon the earth to rise, and with him to raise the body of Adam and the bodies of all the dead; and Christ himself, the Son of God, will be baptized in the river Jordan. When he comes out of the water, he will then anoint your father and all who believe in him with the oil of his mercy. And the oil of mercy shall be from generation to generation for all who are to be reborn of water and the Spirit into eternal life. For then the most beloved Son of God will descend and lead your father into Paradise to the tree of his mercy."

"You, however, go to your father and tell him that the time of his life is fulfilled; and when his soul departs from his body, you will see great wonders in heaven and on earth, and the luminaries of heaven." Saying these things, the archangel Michael immediately departed. And looking into Paradise, Seth saw at the top of the tree a virgin sitting and holding a crucified child in her hands, and Seth marveled greatly. And Eve and Seth returned; and Seth brought back with him aromatic spices, that is, nard, saffron, calamus, and cinnamon.

And when Seth and his mother Eve came to Adam, they told him how the serpent bit his son Seth. And Adam said to his wife, "Behold, what have you done to us? You have brought a great plague and sins upon all your generation. Nevertheless, recount to your children after my death these things you have done and all that has happened to us. For those who shall arise from us, unable to endure their plagues and labors, will curse and revile us, saying, 'Our parents who were from the beginning brought these evils upon us.'"

Hearing these things, Eve began to groan and weep. And Seth said to his father Adam, "My lord father, I saw a wondrous sign in Paradise." And Adam said, "Tell me, my son Seth, what did you see there, so that perhaps I may be able to tell what that wonder signified?" And answering, Seth said to his father Adam, "My father, looking into Paradise I saw at the top of the tree a virgin sitting and holding a crucified child in her hands." Then Adam, looking up to heaven, with bent knees and raising his hands to God, said, "Blessed are you, Lord Father above all, most omnipotent and most merciful God, for now I truly know that a virgin will conceive a son who will die on the cross, through whom we all shall be saved." And Seth revealed to his father Adam all that the archangel Michael had told them near the gates of Paradise. And Adam gave praises to God for all that Seth had told him concerning Michael. And behold, the day of Adam's death arrived, just as Michael, the archangel of God, had foretold.

And when Adam knew that the hour of his death had come, he said to all his sons and daughters, "Behold, now I die, and the number of my years in this world is nine hundred and thirty. But when I am dead, bury me opposite the garden of God in the field of his dwelling." When he had said this, he gave up his spirit. And the sun and moon and stars were darkened for seven days. Now when Seth and his mother Eve had embraced the body of Adam and mourned over it, looking down to the ground with hands clasped over their heads and heads placed upon their knees, and all his sons and daughters were likewise weeping most bitterly, behold, the archangel Michael appeared, standing at Adam's head, and said to Seth, "Arise from your father's body and come to me, so that you may see your father and what the Lord God plans to do with his creature, for he has had mercy on him." And behold, all the angels, playing upon trumpets, said, "Blessed are you, Lord God, for your creature, because you have had mercy on him."

Then Seth saw the hand of the Lord stretched out holding the soul of his father, which he handed over to Michael the archangel, saying, "Let this soul be in your custody in torments until the day of dispensation in the last days, in which I will turn his mourning into joy. Then, indeed, he shall sit upon the throne of him who supplanted him."

And the Lord said again to Michael, "Bring me three fine linen cloths of byssus, and spread one over the body of Adam and another over the body of his son Abel." And all the host of angels went before Adam, and the sleep of his death was sanctified. And the archangels buried the body of Adam and the body of his son Abel in Paradise. Seth and his mother, seeing what was being done by the angels, marveled greatly; and the angels said to them:

"Just as you have seen them buried, in like manner bury your dead." Six days after Adam died, Eve, knowing that her own death was imminent, caused all her sons and daughters to gather, and said to them, "Hear, my sons and daughters, what I shall relate to you. After your father and I had transgressed the commandment of the Lord God, the archangel Michael said to us: 'On account of your transgressions and sins, the Lord will bring the wrath of his judgment upon your race, first by water and later by fire. By these two the Lord will judge the entire human race.'"

"Hear me therefore, my son Seth: make stone tablets and clay tablets of bright earth, and write upon them the whole life of your father and of me, and those things that you have heard and seen from us. For when the Lord judges your race by water, the clay tablets will dissolve and the stone tablets will remain; but when the Lord judges your race by fire, the stone tablets will dissolve and the clay tablets that are baked will remain." And when Eve had said all these things to her children, she spread out her hands, and looking up to heaven, bending her knees to the earth, worshiping the Lord God and giving thanks, she gave up her spirit.

And after great weeping was made, her sons and daughters buried her. And while they were mourning her death for four days, the archangel Michael appeared, saying, "Do not mourn your dead for more than six days, because the seventh day is a sign of the resurrection and the rest of the age to come; and on the seventh day the Lord rested from all his works."

Then Seth made stone tablets and clay tablets of bright earth, and when he had set down the strokes of the letters and written on them the life of his father and of his mother just as he had heard from their recounting and seen with his own eyes, he placed the tablets in the midst of his father's house, in the place of prayer where Adam used to pray to the Lord God. These were seen by many after the flood, but could not be read at all; but the most wise Solomon, after he saw the inscribed stone tablets, prayed to the Lord to open his understanding so that he might comprehend what was written on the tablets. Then an angel of the Lord appeared to him, saying, "I am the angel who held the hand of Seth when he wrote these tablets with his finger with iron. And behold, you shall know the writing so that you will recognize and understand where these stones were; for they were in the place of prayer of Adam where he and his wife used to worship the Lord God. Moreover, you ought to build a house of prayer to the Lord God in that very place." Then Solomon vowed to build a house of prayer to the Lord God in that very place. Then Solomon called those letters achiliacos, that is, written without instruction of lips by the finger of Seth while the angel of the Lord held his hand.

And on those very stones was found what Enoch, the seventh from Adam, prophesied before the flood concerning the coming of Christ Jesus, saying: "Behold, the Lord will come with his holy hosts to execute judgment upon men and to convict all the ungodly concerning all the works that they have done, and concerning all the things that sinners and ungodly murmurers have spoken against him, seeking to speak according to their desires, and their mouth has spoken arrogance."
Adam entered into Paradise after forty days and Eve after eighty, and Adam was in Paradise for seven years and held dominion over all the beasts.

It is to be known that the body of Adam was formed from eight parts. One part was from the clay of the earth, whence his flesh was made, and from this he is sluggish. Another part was from the sea, whence his blood was made, and from this he was wandering and a fugitive. A third part was from the stones of the earth, whence are his bones, and from this he was hard and covetous. A fourth part was from the clouds, whence his thoughts were made, and from this he was made lustful. A fifth part was from the wind, whence his breath was made, and from this he was made fickle. A sixth part was from the sun, whence his eyes were made, and from this he was handsome and radiant. A seventh part is from the light of the world, whence he was made pleasing and from this he has knowledge. An eighth part is from the Holy Spirit, whence his soul was made, and from this come bishops and priests and all the saints and elect of God.

And it is to be known that God made and formed Adam in that place in which Jesus was born, namely in the city of Bethlehem, which is in the center of the world; and there, from the four corners of the earth, the body of Adam was made, with the angels—namely Michael, Gabriel, Raphael, and Uriel—bringing clay of the earth from those regions. And that earth was bright and pure like the sun, and that earth was sprinkled from the four rivers, that is, Gihon, Pishon, Tigris, and Euphrates; and man was made in the image of God, and he breathed into his face the breath of life, namely the soul. For just as he was sprinkled from four rivers, so he received breaths from the four winds.

When Adam had been made and a name had not yet been given to him, the Lord said to the four angels that they should seek a name for him. And Michael went out to the east and saw the eastern star named Ancolim, and took the first letter from it; and Gabriel went out to the south and saw the southern star named Disis, and took the first letter from it; Raphael went out to the north and saw the northern star named Arthos, and took the first letter from it; Uriel went out to the west and saw the western star named Mencembrion, and brought the first letter from it. When these letters had been brought, the Lord said to Uriel, "Read these letters." And he read and said, "Adam." And the Lord said, "Thus let his name be called." Here ends the life of our first-formed Adam and of Eve his wife.
